syllabus.head: First-Order ODEs
syllabus.text: Classification of differential equations, order and degree, variable separable form, reducible to separable form.

syllabus.head: Homogeneous & Reducible Equations
syllabus.text: Homogeneous differential equations, equations reducible to homogeneous form (dy/dx = (ax+by+c)/(a'x+b'y+c')).

syllabus.head: Exact Equations
syllabus.text: Exact differential equations (M dx + N dy = 0, condition (∂M)/(∂y) = (∂N)/(∂x)), integrating factors, equations reducible to exact form.

syllabus.head: Linear Differential Equations
syllabus.text: First-order linear differential equations (dy/dx + Py = Q), equations reducible to linear form (Bernoulli's equation).

syllabus.head: First-Order Higher-Degree Equations
syllabus.text: Equations not of first degree, equations solvable for p (p = dy/dx), equations solvable for y, equations solvable for x, Clairaut's form (y = px + f(p)) and singular solutions.

units.title: Ordinary Differential Equations of Higher Orders

syllabus.head: Linear ODEs with Constant Coefficients
syllabus.text: Higher-order linear differential equations with constant coefficients, complementary functions (CF) for real, distinct, repeated, and complex roots, particular integral (PI) for e<sup>ax</sup>, sin(ax), cos(ax), x<sup>m</sup>, e<sup>ax</sup>V(x), and x V(x).

syllabus.head: Simultaneous Linear Differential Equations
syllabus.text: Systems of linear ODEs with constant coefficients (dx/dt and dy/dt).

syllabus.head: Method of Variation of Parameters
syllabus.text: Second-order ODEs, Wronskian determinant W(y<sub>1</sub>, y<sub>2</sub>), formulas for complete solution.

syllabus.head: Variable Coefficients (Cauchy-Euler & Legendre Forms)
syllabus.text: Cauchy-Euler homogeneous equations (x<sup>2</sup> D<sup>2</sup> + x D), transformation x = e<sup>z</sup>, Legendre linear equations ((ax+b)<sup>2</sup> D<sup>2</sup>).

syllabus.head: Second-Order ODEs with Variable Coefficients
syllabus.text: Method of changing the independent variable, method of removing the first derivative (normal form).

syllabus.head: Sequences & Infinite Series
syllabus.text: Definition of convergence, divergence, and oscillation of series, necessary condition for convergence (limu<sub>n</sub> = 0).

syllabus.head: Tests for Convergence of Positive Term Series
syllabus.text: Comparison test (limit form), D'Alembert's ratio test, Raabe's test, Logarithmic test, Cauchy's root test.

syllabus.head: Alternating Series & Uniform Convergence
syllabus.text: Alternating series, Leibniz's test, absolute and conditional convergence, Weierstrass M-test for uniform convergence.

syllabus.head: Fourier Series
syllabus.text: Periodic functions, Dirichlet's conditions, Euler's formulas for Fourier coefficients (a<sub>0</sub>, a<sub>n</sub>, b<sub>n</sub>), Fourier series in interval (-π, π) and (0, 2π).

syllabus.head: Half-Range Series & Parseval's Theorem
syllabus.text: Half-range Fourier sine and cosine series in (0, π) and (0, L), Parseval's identity/theorem and deductions for series summations (Σ1/n<sup>2</sup>, Σ1/n<sup>4</sup>).

parts.text: Test the convergence of the series x + (2<sup>2</sup> x<sup>2</sup>)/(2!) + (3<sup>3</sup> x<sup>3</sup>)/(3!) + (4<sup>4</sup> x<sup>4</sup>)/(4!) + … (x > 0).
Test the convergence of the series 1<sup>2</sup>/4<sup>2</sup> + 5<sup>2</sup>/8<sup>2</sup> + 9<sup>2</sup>/12<sup>2</sup> + … by Logarithmic test.
Test the convergence of the series 1 + x/2 + (2! x<sup>2</sup>)/3<sup>2</sup> + (3! x<sup>3</sup>)/4<sup>3</sup> + (4! x<sup>4</sup>)/5<sup>4</sup> + ….
Test the convergence or divergence of the series: x/1 + ½x<sup>3</sup>/3 + (1·3)/(2·4)x<sup>5</sup>/5 + (1·3·5)/(2·4·6)x<sup>7</sup>/7 + … (x > 0).
Test for convergence the series 1 + 3/7x + (3·6)/(7·10)x<sup>2</sup> + (3·6·9)/(7·10·13)x<sup>3</sup> + ….
Examine the convergence of the series Σ(³√(n<sup>3</sup> + 1) - n).
Test the convergence of the series Σ<sub>n=1</sub><sup>∞</sup>1/n sin 1/n and Σ<sub>n=1</sub><sup>∞</sup>1/n cos 1/n.
Test the convergence of the series 1/(1·2·3) + 1/(2·3·4) + 1/(3·4·5) + ….
Test the convergence of the series 1/(√1+√2) + 1/(√2+√3) + 1/(√3+√4) + ….
Test the convergence of the series 1/2√1 + x<sup>2</sup>/3√2 + x<sup>4</sup>/4√3 + x<sup>6</sup>/5√4 + ….
Test the convergence of the series whose nth term is 2<sup>n</sup>/n<sup>3</sup> or 3<sup>n</sup>/n<sup>3</sup>.
Test for convergence the series 2<sup>p</sup>/1<sup>q</sup> + 3<sup>p</sup>/2<sup>q</sup> + 4<sup>p</sup>/3<sup>q</sup> + … (p, q > 0).
State and prove Parseval's theorem for Fourier series.
Test the convergence of the alternating series 1 - 1/√2 + 1/√3 - 1/√4 + … using Leibniz's test.
Find the Fourier Series of f(x) = { -π, -π< x < 0 ; x, 0 < x < π }. Hence deduce that π<sup>2</sup>/8 = 1/1<sup>2</sup> + 1/3<sup>2</sup> + 1/5<sup>2</sup> + ….
Find the Fourier series expansion for f(x) = x cos x for -π< x < π.
Find the Fourier series expansion for f(x) = x sin x for -π< x < π. Hence deduce that (π- 2)/4 = 1/(1·3) - 1/(3·5) + 1/(5·7) - ….
Find the Fourier series for f(x) = x + x<sup>2</sup> for -π< x < π. Hence show that π<sup>2</sup>/6 = 1 + 1/2<sup>2</sup> + 1/3<sup>2</sup> + 1/4<sup>2</sup> + ….
If f(x) = x<sup>3</sup> for -π< x < π, determine the values of all the Fourier coefficients.
Find the half-range cosine series of f(x) = x<sup>2</sup> in 0 ≤ x ≤ π.
Find the half-range cosine series of f(x) = |cos x| in (0, π).
If f(x) = { πx, 0 < x < 1 ; π(2 - x), 1 < x < 2 }, use half-range cosine series to show that π<sup>4</sup>/96 = 1/1<sup>4</sup> + 1/3<sup>4</sup> + 1/5<sup>4</sup> + ….
Obtain the Fourier cosine series expansion of f(t) = sin(πt/l) for 0 < t < l.
Find the half-range cosine series to represent f(x) = x for 0 ≤ x ≤ π.

syllabus.head: PDE Formulations & First-Order Equations
syllabus.text: Formation of partial differential equations by elimination of arbitrary constants and arbitrary functions, classification of PDEs (linear, semi-linear, quasi-linear, non-linear).

syllabus.head: First-Order Linear & Non-Linear PDEs
syllabus.text: Lagrange's linear equation (P p + Q q = R), method of characteristics/multipliers, standard forms of non-linear first-order PDEs: f(p, q) = 0, f(z, p, q) = 0, f(x, p) = g(y, q), and Clairaut's form (z = px + qy + f(p, q)).

syllabus.head: Homogeneous Linear PDEs of Higher Order
syllabus.text: Homogeneous linear equations with constant coefficients ((∂<sup>2</sup> z)/(∂x<sup>2</sup>) + a(∂<sup>2</sup> z)/(∂x∂y) + b(∂<sup>2</sup> z)/(∂y<sup>2</sup>) = F(x, y)), complementary function and particular integral evaluation for e<sup>ax+by</sup>, sin(ax+by), cos(ax+by), and x<sup>m</sup> y<sup>n</sup>.

syllabus.head: Applications of PDEs (Separation of Variables)
syllabus.text: Method of separation of variables, complete solution of one-dimensional wave equation ((∂<sup>2</sup> y)/(∂t<sup>2</sup>) = c<sup>2</sup> (∂<sup>2</sup> y)/(∂x<sup>2</sup>)) for vibrating strings, and one-dimensional heat conduction equation ((∂u)/(∂t) = c<sup>2</sup> (∂<sup>2</sup> u)/(∂x<sup>2</sup>)) with physical boundary and initial conditions.

Form the PDE from z = f<sub>1</sub>(y + 2x) + f<sub>2</sub>(y - 3x).
Eliminate arbitrary function f from z = y<sup>2</sup> + 2f(1/x + log y).

A homogeneous rod of conducting material of length l has its ends kept at zero temperature. The temperature at the centre is T and falls uniformly to zero at the two ends. Find the temperature distribution u(x, t).

labs.title: 3D Heat Diffusion & Vibrating String PDE Solver
points: Physical 3D Assets:
Thermal Conduction Mode: 3D cylindrical conducting bar of length L surrounded by insulated lateral walls, with liquid nitrogen chilled ends (0°C).
Vibrating String Mode: 3D elastic string clamped between fixed rigid stanchions at x = 0 and x = L.
Interactive Controls:
Thermal diffusivity slider c<sup>2</sup> and time stepper (t = 0 to 100 s).
Initial thermal profile preset: Symmetrical triangular distribution (peak T at center), uniform u<sub>0</sub>, or parabolic.
Wave propagation velocity slider c and pluck shape controller for string mode.
Real-Time Visual Mechanics:
Thermal Mode: Dynamic color gradient heatmap (Red = Tmax → Yellow → Blue = 0°C) dynamically diffuses across the rod length according to:
Wave Mode: Demonstrates standing wave envelopes (y(x, t) = ΣAn sin nπx/L cos nπct/L), illustrating nodes and antinodes in 3D space.

syllabus.head: Complex Functions & Analyticity
syllabus.text: Functions of a complex variable (f(z) = u + iv), limit, continuity, differentiability, analytic functions, necessary and sufficient conditions for analyticity (Cauchy-Riemann equations in Cartesian and polar forms).

syllabus.head: Harmonic Functions
syllabus.text: Laplace's equation (∇<sup>2</sup> u = 0), harmonic functions, harmonic conjugate (v(x, y)), Milne-Thomson method for constructing analytic functions.

syllabus.head: Complex Integration
syllabus.text: Line integrals in the complex plane, Cauchy-Goursat theorem, Cauchy's integral formula for functions and higher derivatives.

syllabus.head: Singularities, Residues & Contour Integration
syllabus.text: Singular points, classification of singularities (isolated, pole of order m, essential singularity, removable singularity), calculation of residues at poles, Cauchy's Residue theorem.
Evaluation of real definite integrals using unit circle contour method: ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>2π</sup> f(cos θ, sin θ) dθ and ∫<sub>-∞</sub><sup>∞</sup>f(x) dx.

parts.text: Show that the function u = ½ log(x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup>) is harmonic, and find its harmonic conjugate v(x, y).
Show that the function u = x<sup>3</sup> - 3xy<sup>2</sup> is harmonic, find its harmonic conjugate, and determine the corresponding analytic function f(z).
Prove that the function u = e<sup>-x</sup>(x sin y - y cos y) is harmonic.
Find the analytic function whose imaginary part is v = e<sup>-x</sup>(x cos y + y sin y).
Determine the analytic function f(z) = u + iv such that u - v = e<sup>x</sup>(cos y - sin y).
Let f(z) = u + iv be analytic. If u = 3x - 2xy, find v and express f(z) in terms of z.
Find values of a and b such that f(z) = x<sup>2</sup> + a y<sup>2</sup> - 2xy + i(b x<sup>2</sup> - y<sup>2</sup> + 2xy) is analytic.
Show that the function f(z) = e<sup>-z<sup>-4</sup></sup> for z ≠ 0 and f(0) = 0 is not analytic at z = 0, although Cauchy-Riemann equations are satisfied at that point. Explain why.
Show that the function e<sup>x</sup>(cos y + i sin y) is analytic and find its derivative.
Evaluate by Cauchy's integral formula: ∮<sub>C</sub> dz/(z(z + πi)) where C is the circle |z + 3i| = 1.
Evaluate ∮<sub>C</sub> (z - 1)/((z + 1)<sup>2</sup> (z - 2)) dz where C is the circle |z - i| = 2.
Evaluate ∮<sub>C</sub> (4 - 3z)/(z(z - 1)(z - 2)) dz where |z| = 3/2.
Evaluate ∮<sub>C</sub> e<sup>z</sup>/(z<sup>2</sup> + 1) dz over the path |z| = 2.
Evaluate ∫<sub>1-i</sub><sup>2+3i</sup> (z<sup>2</sup> + z)dz along the straight line joining (1, -1) and (2, 3).
Find the value of ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>1+i</sup> (x - y + ix<sup>2</sup>)dz: (i) along the straight line from z = 0 to z = 1+i, (ii) along the real axis to z = 1 and then vertically to z = 1+i.
Evaluate ∫<sub>C</sub> |z| dz where C is the straight line from z = -i to z = i.
State and prove Cauchy's Residue theorem.
Evaluate ∮<sub>C</sub> z<sup>2</sup>/((z - 1)<sup>2</sup> (z + 2)) dz where |z| = 3.
Evaluate the residues of z<sup>2</sup>/((z - 1)(z - 2)(z - 3)) at z = 1, 2, 3 and infinity, and hence evaluate the closed contour integral.
Apply Cauchy Residue theorem to evaluate ∮<sub>C</sub> (3z<sup>2</sup> + z + 1)/((z<sup>2</sup> - 1)(z + 3)) dz where |z| = 2.
Find the sum of the residues of f(z) = (sin z)/(z cos z) at its poles inside |z| = 2.
Evaluate ∮<sub>C</sub> e<sup>z</sup>/((z<sup>2</sup> + π<sup>2</sup>)<sup>2</sup>) dz where C is |z| = 4.
Prove that ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>2π</sup> dθ/(a + b cos θ) = 2π/(√(a<sup>2</sup> - b<sup>2</sup>)) (a > b > 0).
Evaluate by contour integration: ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>2π</sup> dθ/(2 + cos θ).
Solve by contour integration: ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>2π</sup> dθ/(3 + cos θ).
Prove that ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>π</sup> (a dθ)/(a<sup>2</sup> + sin<sup>2</sup>θ) = π/(√(1 + a<sup>2</sup>)) (a > 0).
Evaluate ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>2π</sup> dθ/(a + b sin θ) where a > |b|.
Evaluate ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>2π</sup> (cos 2θ)/(5 + 4 cos θ) dθ.
Evaluate ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>2π</sup> sin<sup>2</sup>θ/(5 - 4 cos θ) dθ.

labs.title: 3D Complex Residue & Contour Integral Vector Engine
points: Physical 3D Assets:
Complex Argand plane (x, y) mapped onto a 3D topographic relief surface where elevation represents the magnitude |f(z)| and surface texture/color represents the phase arg(f(z)).
Interactive 3D closed contour loop C (circular or arbitrary shape) rendered as a floating path over the complex terrain.
Interactive Controls:
Function selector: Rational functions with simple and repeated poles (e.g., f(z) = z<sup>2</sup>/((z-1)<sup>2</sup>(z+2))).
Contour center (x<sub>0</sub>, y<sub>0</sub>) and radius slider R (|z - z<sub>0</sub>| = R).
Trigonometric contour integration preset (z = e<sup>iθ</sup>, dθ= dz/iz).
Real-Time Visual Mechanics:
Poles appear as vertical chimneys shooting up to infinity (|f(z)| → ∞).
As the contour loop expands or moves across the complex plane, it detects enclosed singular points; triggers an animation of local winding residues at each enclosed pole.
Evaluates and displays the closed contour integral in real time:
Directly outputs the analytical and numerical solution for real definite integrals like ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>2π</sup> dθ/(a + b cos θ), matching exam questions.
